title: Design is choosing
question: What is a designer actually doing?
reading: Before AI came up at all, the readings described design as a run of decisions, each one closing off others. The class took that further: choices are never neutral, and how good they are depends on how much you know.

views.label: Every choice rules others out
There is no recipe, only a way of thinking
You are only as intentional as you are informed
Knowing the history shows there is a choice

mine.quote: we are all designers and makers of the forms in which things present themselves to us

title: What taste is
question: If a machine can make the options, what is taste for?
reading: The industry line is that AI does the work and designers bring taste. In class, taste turned out to mean something you can explain and test against real people, not a private feeling.

views.label: Taste grows by explaining why
Taste is knowing what helps the user
Taste is shared, and trust has to be earned

mine.quote: I should have prioritized my time to solve bigger problems and dig deeper

title: What to hand off
question: Which decisions should a designer give away?
reading: None of these responses argue for refusing AI. The question is where to draw the line, and most people drew it around the decisions: define the problem, keep the judgment, let the tool execute.

views.label: Keep the decisions, use the tool
Define the problem before the tool
Knowledge is what directs the tool

mine.quote: I felt anxiety that I had lost control on what it was and was not deleting

title: What a prompt leaves out
question: Who makes the choices a prompt doesn’t?
reading: Twelve of the twenty classmates quoted Ted Chiang’s essay, more than any other writing about AI. His point is about quantity: a prompt holds a few choices, a finished piece holds thousands, and the model makes the rest.

views.label: Art is made of many choices
A new medium earns its place through choices
The model fills in what you skip

mine.quote: a step above a high-fidelity prototype but live for people to access

title: Growth needs the struggle
question: What do we lose when the work gets easy?
reading: This is where the argument turns from the work to the person making it. If the hard part is skipped, so is the learning that the hard part produces.

views.label: Skipping the work skips the growth
Working in the medium is the point
Everyone ends up knowing the same surface

mine.quote: I am very new to the coding world and have been learning a lot and pushing myself

title: What stays ours
question: Is the work, and the responsibility for it, still ours?
reading: The last weeks asked who owns a result that draws on everyone’s work, and who answers for it. The answers ranged from worry about lost styles to the reminder that people have always remixed.

views.label: Distinct styles get absorbed
People remix too, so where is the line?
There is less intention in the world
Responsibility feels far away, but it stays
Our tools shape us back

mine.quote: what do we actually own? is everything rented now?
